newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-DRAVID AND GANGULY BREATHE LIFE BACK INTO INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DRAVID AND GANGULY BREATHE LIFE BACK INTO INDIA.

text.p: An unbroken fourth wicket stand of 133 between Rahul Dravid and Saurav Ganguly rescued India from the doldrums on the opening day of the third and final test against South Africa on Thursday.
The pair took India from 100 for three in mid-afternoon to 233 for three at the close and were responsible for ensuring the touring team did not squander first use of a perfect pitch.
Dravid was the more circumspect of the two, reaching his 50 off 133 balls. By contrast the left-handed Ganguly blasted 46 of his first 50 in boundaries, hitting 10 fours and a six from 89 balls.
By the close Dravid (81) had hit 11 fours from 201 balls and Ganguly (68) 12 fours and a six from 119 balls.
India scored just 117 runs in the first two sessions and seemed to be settling for grinding out a morale boosting draw after losing the first two tests by huge margins.
Opening pair Nayan Mongia and Vikram Rathore had crawled to 25 from 22 overs against an off target South African seam attack before the introduction of spin heralded the breakthrough.
Left-arm wrist spinner Paul Adams had Rathore caught behind with his first ball after the recalled opener had scored 13 from 69 balls.
At lunch India were 41 for one and shortly afterwards it became 46 for two when Allan Donald defeated Mongia's defensive prod and hit the middle stump. Mongia needed 104 balls to score 21.

India captain Sachin Tendulkar raised the tempo with seven boundaries but, looking for an eighth, he drove loosely at Hansie Cronje's fourth delivery and was caught at second slip by Brian McMillan for 35.
South Africa's frustration was complete when Donald was forced to leave the field after one ball of his 19th over with a troublesome right ankle.
